text:
ingrid (sre): noticed a sawtooth pattern of latency + 502s hitting hosted inference in eu-central-az1, started ~10:05UTC. customers reporting timeouts and auth retries.
juan (neteng): looking at peering telemetry now, seeing intermittent packet loss on peer ASN 64544, microbursts every ~30s.
mike (support): Customer ACME reported 502s for 3 minutes, then normal for 20s, then spike again. They provided request ids: req_8a2f, req_b3d9. Billing impact flagged (token overage alerts).
olivia (oncall): can we confirm region-level fallback kicked in for some routes? Any auto-failover events?
telemetry-bot: alert: hosted-inference.eu-central-az1.502_rate > 5% for 3m; p50 latency rose 120ms -> 650ms; kv-cache miss rate +12%.
juan (neteng): running `mtr -r -c 20 10.32.18.1` to nearest edge -> shows 2-4% packet loss at hop 5 (peer uplink). sample: `Loss% Last Avg Best Wrst StDev 0.0 0.2 0.1 1.2 0.4` but hop5 3/20 lost.
ingrid (sre): stack traces show connections hanging in gateway proxy while waiting for backend tokens; downstream got 502 from edge. snippet from gateway logs: ```[2026-02-12T10:06:12Z] WARN route=eu-central-az1 path=peer-64544 conn_wait 230ms upstream_err=502 code=ECONNRESET```
mike (support): customer ticket updated: "timeouts hit during peak batch tests, now partial recovery but still flapping." they asked for mitigation ETA.
juan (neteng): opened ticket with provider ASN 64544, they see transient bufferbloat and are investigating queuing on their egress. provisional root cause: microburst-induced packet drops causing TCP retransmit & head-of-line delays.
olivia (oncall): mitigation options: 1) force cross-AZ routing to eu-central-az2 for new sessions (soft-failover), 2) temporarily reduce batch sizes / lower max_inflight to reduce tail latency, 3) pin high-SLA customers to dedicated capacity. Thoughts?
ingrid (sre): start with option 2 and 1 (in that order). push a config change to lower `max_decoder_inflight` from 8 -> 4 for eu-central-az1 pools. rolling canary first.
deploy-bot: rollout started: config/eu-central-az1/inference-pools max_decoder_inflight -> 4 (canary group 5% traffic). uid: roll_1761239876.
telemetry-bot: canary metrics: 5% group p95 latency down 18%, 502 rate down from 6.2% -> 1.1% within 90s.
juan (neteng): provider responded: queued a soft-priority scheduling tweak on their egress, should take ~15m to converge. they asked us to keep flows stable (avoid large bursts).
mike (support): communicated to ACME: mitigation applied (reduced inflight + canary). monitoring closely, ops investigating provider update.
olivia (oncall): scheduling cross-AZ sticky routing for new sessions disabled to avoid extra hairpin. we've queued a policy to prefer az2 for customers with >20 RPS until provider reconverges.
ingrid (sre): will keep thread open. if 502s <1% for 30m we close. leaving notes for postmortem: - provider microbursts on ASN64544 - autoscaling/batching interaction amplified tail - recommend future: adaptive inflight and prefix-KV warmup.
mike (support): noted for ticket: reproducible sawtooth pattern, provided logs, steps we took, and customer notification copy.
juan (neteng): follow-up: asking provider for BGP dump and interface counters for the 10:04-10:14UTC window. saving pcap sample from edge for postmortem.
ingrid (sre): thanks all. marking sev3 -> monitoring. will escalate to sev2 if 502s spike again. :white_check_mark:
